**Where we are ahead:** the only FHE scheme found for Zig, pure Zig with `std` offering none (and `paillier` additively homomorphic only); exact-integer BFV that adds and multiplies to a bounded depth with relinearization and a noise-budget report. **Where we are even:** the BFV core that SEAL, OpenFHE and Lattigo also carry (keygen, encrypt, decrypt, add, multiply) and SEAL's default parameter/NTT design, but no SEAL vectors have been produced or checked in, so this is a design match, not a verified interop. Also even with SEAL's BFV API: plaintext operands (`addPlain`/`subPlain`/`mulPlain`/`mulScalar`/`negate`), CRT-slot batching in SEAL's `2 × N/2` slot layout with row rotations and the row swap (`applyGalois`), modulus switching (`modSwitchToNext`), SEAL's `BFVDefault` prime chains at 128/192/256 bits (`params.secure`), and versioned byte codecs for every key and ciphertext (a format of our own, not SEAL's). **Where we are behind:** BGV and CKKS, bootstrapping (see Roadmap); rotation by an arbitrary step needs the key for that step (SEAL composes power-of-two keys); the codecs carry no compression and are not SEAL's wire format.

## What this module is

A leveled **BFV** (Brakerski/Fan–Vercauteren, IACR ePrint 2012/144)
homomorphic-encryption scheme over the RLWE ring `R_q = Z_q[X]/(X^N+1)`, in
Residue-Number-System (RNS) form, following Microsoft SEAL's parameter/NTT
design. *Leveled* = supports a bounded multiplicative depth; **no bootstrapping**
(the depth-refresh step) in this arc. BFV rather than BGV or CKKS: BFV is
exact-integer (no CKKS approximate-rescaling encoding to reason about), the
plaintext/ciphertext scaling is fully specified, and it is Microsoft SEAL's
default — so a byte-exact cross-check target exists. BGV is close but its
modulus-switching noise bookkeeping is a second, orthogonal source of subtlety;
BFV's single `⌊t/q·…⌉` rescale is the cleaner *first* FHE. CKKS (approximate)
and BGV are deferred increments.

## Scheme choice — BFV vs BGV (justification)

| | BFV (chosen) | BGV |
|---|---|---|
| Plaintext placement | scaled by `Δ=⌊q/t⌋` in the high bits | in the low bits (mod `t`) |
| Noise control on mul | one `⌊t/q·…⌉` rescale | modulus-switch chain (extra bookkeeping) |
| Cross-check oracle | **SEAL default** (byte-exact target *in principle* — see below) | HElib (less canonical as a "default") |
| Encoding | exact integer | exact integer |

Both are exact-integer leveled schemes of the same difficulty class; BFV wins
on *fewest independent noise-management mechanisms to get right first* and on
SEAL being available as a canonical KAT oracle **for tiering purposes** — this
row is a *could-be-anchored* argument for why BFV is not Fable-tier, not a
claim that a SEAL KAT has been run. No SEAL vectors exist in this repo; see
"Anchors (verification harness)" below for what is actually checked.

## Layers

- **Arithmetic backbone:** `modarith` + `ntt` + `rns` + `ring` + `encode` + `params`, byte-exact-KAT'd.
- **Scheme core:** `bfv.Bfv` — `keyGen` / `encrypt` / `decrypt` / `add` / `sub`; textbook leveled BFV over the RNS ring.
- **Noise-management core:** `mul` (tensor + `⌊t/q·…⌉` rescale) + `genRelinKey` / `relinearize` (relin-key key-switch) + `noiseBudget`.

`gate.zig` holds two switches (`scheme_core_implemented`, `fable_core_implemented`), both `true`; the tests of the scheme layer skip while one is `false`.

Not part of the module (see *Backlog / deferred*): bootstrapping, CKKS/BGV, Galois rotations and CRT-slot SIMD batch encoding, modulus switching, byte codecs, plaintext-operand ops. The `rns.Basis` helpers ship only the exact O(reconstruct) base conversion; the fast one lives with the scheme layer (`mulBehz`), where its bounds are checkable against `P`.

## Which layers have an external anchor

- **NTT / RNS / encode:** textbook and byte-exact-KAT-able: a forward/inverse NTT on a fixed polynomial is deterministic and cross-checked against a re-derivation and against an independent schoolbook convolution (see *Anchors*).
- **`keyGen` / `encrypt` / `decrypt`:** a construction for which byte-exact SEAL vectors could exist, but **no SEAL vectors have been produced or run** (the module has no `data/` directory); what validates this layer is `Dec(Enc(·))` round-trips against `encode.addRef`/`mulRef`, and scripted-draw KATs for the draws. The decrypt `⌊t/q·(c0+c1·s)⌉` rounding is the only noise-adjacent piece and has no external anchor either.
- **`mul` + `relinearize` + `noiseBudget`:** no simple anchor for the hard part. Self-consistent tests can pass while noise is silently mismanaged (a multiply that works for tiny inputs but whose noise growth is wrong and fails at depth; a key-switch that decrypts subtly wrong; a rescale that rounds the wrong way), and ciphertext noise is randomised, so end-to-end correctness at depth is the only real test. That is why the multiply parameters are sized by a worst-case ledger (see *Multiply*).

## Anchors (verification harness)

Two anchor families, per the plan:

1. **NTT/RNS byte-exact KAT (the deterministic anchor).** `kat_vectors.zig`
   holds vectors from an INDEPENDENT Python re-derivation (a from-scratch
   textbook NTT + CRT, not this module's code — see "External-reference
   anchoring"). `forward_a` pins the forward transform's exact output
   (bit-reversed order); `negamul_ab` pins the canonical negacyclic product
   (order-independent). The Zig NTT must reproduce both, AND must equal the
   in-module independent schoolbook negacyclic convolution over random inputs
   (a fully independent algorithm — the strongest anti-self-consistency check
   for the transform). RNS CRT reconstruction is pinned on primes `{17,97}`.
2. **Homomorphic property end-to-end (the strong anchor).** `Dec(Enc(a)⊕Enc(b))
   == a+b (mod t)`, `Dec(relin(Enc(a)⊗Enc(b))) == a·b (mod t)`, and a
   multiply-DEPTH `a·b·c` that still decrypts (exercises the noise budget) — all
   decrypt against the `encode.mulRef`/`addRef` plaintext-space references.
   These defeat self-consistent-but-wrong. The
   mul/depth anchors run over random AND boundary (all-`t−1`) plaintexts on
   `params.test_mul` — see *Multiply* below for why not `test_tiny`.

**Deliberately-broken positive controls:**

- *Cyclic-vs-negacyclic discriminator* — builds the WRONG (`X^N=+1` cyclic)
  ring product with no NTT code, confirms it differs from the negacyclic answer,
  and confirms the real NTT matches the negacyclic (not the cyclic) one. Proves
  the `mulNegacyclic == mulSchoolbook` anchor would have caught a cyclic-NTT
  bug.
- *Wrong-scale "encryptor"* — using ONLY the real ring arithmetic (no scheme
  core), constructs a noiseless toy ciphertext with the correct scale
  (`c0+c1·s == Δ·m`) and one with a dropped scale (`Δ'=1`); the structural
  `scaleCheck` ACCEPTS the correct one and REJECTS the wrong one. Proves the
  scaling/noise anchor bites independently of `encrypt`/`decrypt` — this is exactly
  the dropped-`Δ` bug class the multiply must not commit.

## Multiply: exact-tensor path + worst-case noise ledger

Design decisions of `mul`/`genRelinKey`/`relinearize`/`noiseBudget` and the noise argument, for audit:

- **Exact integer tensor (the correctness crux).** The tensor
  `(c0d0, c0d1+c1d0, c1d1)` must be the EXACT integer product of fixed
  representatives (centered here, to halve the noise constants) before the
  per-component `⌊t/q·T_i⌉` rescale. This is forced: the rescale does not
  commute with mod-`q` reduction (`⌊t/q·[T]_q⌉` differs from `[⌊t/q·T⌉]_q` by
  `t·k ≢ 0 (mod q)`), so a "stay in RNS, multiply in the ring, then rescale"
  shortcut decrypts to garbage.
- **How the exact tensor is obtained — three paths, one value.** `mulExactRef`
  is the `O(N²)` schoolbook over an exact integer (the ORACLE). `mulRnsNtt`
  computes it in an auxiliary RNS basis sized so the centered CRT lift is exact
  (`O(num_aux·N log N)`), then still rescales by big-integer division.
  **`mulBehz`** is the BEHZ/HPS path: the tensor stays in residues (main basis,
  an auxiliary sub-basis, and one redundant modulus `m̃`) and the rescale is an
  exact RNS division chain followed by a Shenoy–Kumaresan base extension — the
  exact integer is never materialised and no big-integer division happens. It
  is EXACT, not approximate: the only inequalities it rests on are
  `∏p > 2·div_shift` and `num_rs < m̃`, both comptime-checked, and the
  differential test asserts bit-identity with `mulExactRef` at
  `log q ∈ {11, 36, 120, 300}` including saturating inputs. `mul` picks the
  path by a MEASURED rule (`Bfv.behz_min_tensor_bits`): BEHZ as soon as
  `TensorI` outgrows a native 128-bit integer, which is exactly where LLVM
  stops lowering the constant-divisor division to a multiply.
- **Why the rescale keeps the scale at `Δ`.** With `ct_i(s) = Δm_i + v_i +
  q·r_i` over the integers and `tΔ = q − r_t`: `(t/q)·ct1(s)ct2(s) ≡
  Δ[m1m2]_t + (m1v2+m2v1) + t(r1v2+r2v1) − r_t(…small…) + ⌊·⌉-error (mod q)`
  — one `Δ` is cancelled by `t/q`, the `q·[…]` cross terms collapse to
  `t·(r_i·v_j)` (the dominant growth), and `q²r1r2` vanishes mod `q`.
- **Relin correctness.** `rlk_i = (−(a_i·s+e_i) + w^i·s², a_i)`, `w = 2^relin_base_log2` (a `Params` field, default 8; the security-grade set uses 55, so 4 rows);
  `relinearize` digit-decomposes `c2 = Σ w^i d_i` exactly and adds
  `Σ d_i·rlk_i`, so the phase gains `Σ d_i(w^i s² − e_i) + Σ d_i a_i s −
  Σ d_i a_i s = c2·s² − Σ d_i e_i` — the `c2·s²` term is replaced by the same
  value under `s`, up to key-switch noise `≤ relin_digits·N·(w−1)`.
- **Depth-2 is a worst-case guarantee, not a probabilistic pass.** The mul
  anchors run on `params.test_mul` (`N=16`, `t=16`, `q ≈ 2^35.6`) because
  `test_tiny`'s `q = 1649` cannot hold even one multiply (worst-case cross
  term alone exceeds `q`). On `test_mul` the full ledger (params.zig) bounds
  depth-2 noise at `≈ 5.7e8 < Δ/2 ≈ 1.61e9` (≈2.8× margin) for ANY seed and
  ANY plaintexts including all-`(t−1)` — which answers the
  "verifiability risk" caveat below for these parameters: the depth anchor is
  deterministic teeth, not a lucky seed.

## External-reference anchoring

The NTT/RNS KAT vectors were produced by a standalone Python script that
re-implements the textbook negacyclic NTT (Cooley-Tukey forward with
`zetas[k]=psi^bitrev(k)`, Gentleman-Sande inverse + `N^-1`) and CRT from
scratch, self-checking `intt(ntt(x))==x` and `ntt_mul==schoolbook` before
emitting the Zig arrays now in `kat_vectors.zig`. It shares no code with this
module. Matching it byte-exact defeats "self-consistent but nonstandard": a NTT
that reconstructs but transforms in a different convention cannot match
`forward_a`. Per CONVENTIONS.md §5 this needs no `NOTICE` entry (a public
paper/spec is not a copyrightable work; no third-party source was ported).

## Plaintext operands, batching, rotations, modulus switching, codecs

- **Plaintext operands.** `addPlain`/`subPlain` add/subtract `Δ·m` to `c0`, the
  same scaled plaintext `encrypt` uses. `mulPlain` multiplies every component by
  `m` lifted to `R_q` with coefficients in `[0,t)` (SEAL's `multiply_plain`):
  the phase becomes `(Δa + v)·m`, i.e. `Δ·(a·m mod t)` plus `v·m` plus an
  `r_t`-sized carry per multiple of `t` folded away; noise grows by at most
  `‖m‖₁ ≤ N(t−1)`. `mulScalar(k)` is the same with the constant `k mod t`.
- **Batching (`batch.zig`).** For a prime `t ≡ 1 (mod 2N)` the plaintext ring
  splits into `N` slots `m(ζ^e)`, `e` odd. Layout as SEAL's `BatchEncoder`: row
  0 column `i` at `e = 3^i`, row 1 at `e = −3^i (mod 2N)`. `encodeSlots`/
  `decodeSlots` are one inverse/forward NTT mod `t`; the output position of
  each slot is found at `init` by transforming the polynomial `X` (its
  transform is the list of evaluation points), so the layout does not depend
  on the NTT's output order. A slot value `≥ t` is refused, as SEAL refuses it.
- **Galois rotations.** `σ_g: X ↦ X^g` (`g` odd, `< 2N`) maps slot `e` to slot
  `e·g`: `g = 3^k` rotates both rows left by `k` (`galoisElement(k)`, negative
  `k` rotates right), `g = 2N − 1` swaps the rows (`galois_row_swap`) — SEAL's
  `rotate_rows`/`rotate_columns`. `applyGalois` applies `σ_g` to both
  components and key-switches `σ_g(c1)` from `σ_g(s)` back to `s` with a
  `GaloisKey`, whose rows are built exactly like the relinearisation key's with
  target `σ_g(s)` instead of `s²` (`genSwitchRows`), and consumed by the same
  digit decomposition (`keySwitchAccumulate`), so the added noise is the relin
  bound `relin_digits·N·(w−1)`. One key per element: no composition of
  power-of-two keys.
- **Modulus switching.** `modSwitchToNext` divides and rounds by the last prime
  (`c' = ⌊(c + ⌊q_L/2⌋)/q_L⌋`, computed per limb as `(c_i + ⌊q_L/2⌋ − r)·q_L^{-1}`
  with `r = (c_L + ⌊q_L/2⌋) mod q_L`: SEAL's `divide_and_round_q_last`). The
  result belongs to `Bfv(params.dropLast(P))` (`Next`): the parameter set is
  comptime, so a level is a type. It decrypts under `modSwitchSecretKey(sk)`
  (the same `s`, one limb fewer) with noise `≈ v/q_L + (1 + ‖s‖₁)/2`.
- **Byte codecs.** `"ZBFV"`, a version byte, an object kind, then the full
  parameter fingerprint (`N`, `L`, `t`, the primes, `relin_base_log2`), then
  the object's rings as coefficient-domain `u64` residues, little-endian. A
  decoder refuses another parameter set, a version or kind it does not know, a
  residue `≥ q_i`, a wrong length, a component count outside `{2,3}` and an
  invalid Galois element, so every decoded value is one an encoder could have
  produced for this `P`. The secret key is decoded into an out-parameter, and
  its residues are range-checked without an early exit. SEAL's own format
  (with zlib/zstd compression) is not reproduced.
- **Standard parameter chains.** `params.defaultPrimes(n, level)` returns the
  primes of SEAL 4.x `CoeffModulus::BFVDefault` (its
  `default_coeff_modulus_128/192/256` tables, MIT) for `n = 1024 … 32768`;
  `params.maxLogQ` is the HomomorphicEncryption.org maximum `log2 q`
  (`CoeffModulus::MaxBitCount`). The tests re-check every chain (prime,
  `≡ 1 mod 2n`, SEAL's total width, within the standard) instead of trusting
  the table. `params.secure(n, t, level)` builds a `Params` from them with a
  relinearisation base of one digit per prime (one bit under the smallest
  prime's width) when the chain has two or more primes. One-prime chains
  (`n ≤ 2048`, and `n = 4096` at 256 bits) are, as in SEAL, too small for
  key switching with a large `t`.

## Reuse map (dedup)

- **`std.crypto` NTT (ML-KEM/ML-DSA):** NOT reusable — hardwired to `q=3329`
  (`i16`), no exported generic ring/NTT. BFV needs word-size (~30–60-bit) RNS
  primes, so a fresh `u128`-product NTT was built (mirroring the in-repo
  `falcon` negacyclic NTT structure, which is likewise degree-generic mod a
  fixed 12289 — the *shape* was followed, not the modulus).
- **`std.crypto.ff.Modulus`** (used by `paillier`/`rsa`/`vdf`): a fixed-width
  constant-time Montgomery type aimed at big RSA-class moduli — heavier than the
  single-word NTT-prime arithmetic here; `modarith.zig` stays word-sized `u64`.
- **`paillier`** is additively homomorphic only (no ciphertext multiply); BFV is
  a different scheme, not an extension of it.
- Net: FHE is largely self-contained (RLWE over `Z_q[X]/(X^N+1)`), so this
  module depends on `std` plus the sibling `entropy` (only for `SecureSource`), with its own `modarith`/`ntt`/`rns`.

## Threats / caveats (Part 1)

- **Security status.** `test_tiny` / `test_mul` / `bfv_toy` remain
  correctness-only toy parameters and claim nothing.
  `params.sec_n8192_logq218` is the one set with a security claim: `N = 8192`,
  four NTT primes totalling `log2 q = 218.000`, `t = 65537`, ternary secret —
  the shape the HomomorphicEncryption.org tables give for ~128-bit classical
  security. What is VERIFIED here is correctness at those parameters (a depth-2
  evaluation over boundary + random plaintexts decrypts exactly, and the
  worst-case ledger in `params.zig` guarantees depth 4); the ~128-bit figure is
  a citation of the standard tables, **not** a lattice estimate run in this
  repo. There is also no side-channel hardening beyond the boundary in
  "Partially constant-time" below — so this is a set to benchmark and reason
  about, not one to deploy behind. The same holds for `params.secure`'s chains:
  the security level is SEAL's/the standard's table, cited, not estimated.
- **The entropy seam is typed, not documented.** `keyGen`, `encrypt` and
  `genRelinKey` take `io: std.Io` and draw through `entropy.SecureSource`
  (`modules/entropy`), the fail-closed `std.Random` adapter over
  `std.Io.randomSecure` — not `std.Random.IoSource`, which binds the
  silently-degrading `std.Io.random`. They deliberately do NOT take
  `std.Random` directly: that is a vtable, its quality cannot be read at the
  call site, and `DefaultPrng.init(0).random()` looks exactly like a correct
  argument. The consequence of getting it wrong is not a weaker instance —
  with `u,e0,e1` predictable an attacker computes `c0 − p0·u − e0 = Δ·m` and reads the
  plaintext **without the secret key**, and `genRelinKey` publishes `s²` to the
  evaluator under masks the evaluator can reproduce. The `…ForTest` twins keep
  `std.Random` so the KATs (including the scripted-word test that pins which
  draws `keyGen` makes, in order) stay reproducible; the name is the only thing
  separating them from the production path, and `bfv.zig`'s "RNG seam" tests pin
  both halves of that split at comptime.
- **Partially constant-time — read the boundary, do not round it up.**
  What IS source-level constant time: the ternary sampler (`sampleTernary`
  draws with the fixed-cost `uintLessThanBiased` instead of a rejection loop and
  selects the trit with an arithmetic mask, so neither the draw nor the store
  branches on the secret), and the word-arithmetic leaves every secret-bearing
  product routes through (`addMod`/`subMod`/`Modulus.mul`/`Shoup.mul` end in a
  masked conditional subtract, `modarith.csub` — its mask, and `subMod`'s, laundered through an asm `blackBox` on every target, because on baseline x86-64 (`-mcpu=x86_64`) LLVM otherwise compiles it to `cmp`/`jb` in the Shoup NTT butterflies on secret-key products (the portable ctgrind run reads `keygen` 4 and `decrypt` 2 in-file with the barrier; native is unaffected) — and there is no `%q` division, which had
  data-dependent latency on some µarch).
  What is NOT, and is not claimed to be: `powMod`/`invMod`/`primitive2NthRoot`/
  the auxiliary-prime search are public-data setup and remain variable-time;
  `sampleUniform` still uses the rejection-based `uintLessThan` (its output is
  a public mask, not a secret); `decrypt`/`noiseBudget`/`centerRaw`/
  `auxResidues` branch on reconstructed coefficient values; `relinearize`'s
  digit decomposition is value-shaped; and the entropy source behind
  `std.Io.randomSecure` is the host's, so its timing is outside our control
  (as is a `std.Random` handed to one of the `…ForTest` twins). Above all this is
  **source-level** CT — the compiler may
  rematerialise a branch from a mask, and nothing here is verified codegen or a
  microarchitectural claim.
- **No fixed integer width remains.** `Bfv.QU` (the `[0,q)` value and CRT
  accumulator) and `Bfv.TensorI` are both derived from the parameter set, so
  `log q` is not capped by a native integer width. `params.sec_n8192_logq218` (`N = 8192`, `log q = 218`,
  `t = 65537`) builds and evaluates a depth-2 circuit exactly — see "Security
  status" above. `decrypt`/`noiseBudget` still reconstruct a wide integer per
  coefficient (that is inherent to `⌊t/q·…⌉` at decrypt time); the MULTIPLY no
  longer does.
- **Verifiability risk:** BFV
  ciphertext noise is randomised, so the multiply's correctness at depth
  has no byte-exact external KAT — the noise-budget accounting is exactly the
  piece with no external deterministic anchor. The multiply answers it by SIZING the mul-anchor parameters so that the
  worst-case noise ledger (params.zig `test_mul`) guarantees depth-2
  correctness for every seed — turning the probabilistic property back into a
  deterministic test (see *Multiply* above).

## Verification

- **Run:** `scripts/modtest bfv`. Opt-in benchmark (old-path vs new-path ns/op, `src/bench.zig`): `BFV_BENCH=1 scripts/lib/capped zig build test-bfv -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`.
- **Test classes:**
  - arithmetic leaves (`modarith`, `ntt`, `rns`, `ring`, `encode`, `params` validation), each against a division-based or schoolbook reference kept in the module as the differential oracle;
  - byte-exact KATs from the independent re-derivation (NTT at `q = 17` and `q = 97`, RNS CRT) — see *Anchors* and *External-reference anchoring*;
  - the deliberately-broken positive controls (cyclic vs negacyclic, wrong-scale "encryptor", corrupted relin key);
  - scripted-draw KATs that pin which random draws `keyGen`, `genRelinKey` and `encrypt` make and that the key-generation error `e`, each relin-key row's `e_i`, the encryption errors and `Δ` land in the output (decryption cannot see these), plus ternary-sampler and `sampleUniform` range tests;
  - decrypt rounding and `noiseBudget` KATs with exact values (including `t = 5` and a 3-component product);
  - homomorphic add, mul+relin and multiply-depth end to end over random and boundary plaintexts on `test_mul`, a depth-2 evaluation on the security-grade set, and an enc/dec round-trip at `bfv_toy` (`N = 1024`);
  - the three multiply paths (`mulExactRef`, `mulRnsNtt`, `mulBehz`) bit-identical at `log q ∈ {11, 36, 120, 300}`, including saturating inputs;
  - `ops_test.zig`: plaintext operands, batch-encoded row rotations / row swap / slot-wise product, modulus switching, codec round-trips and every decoder refusal, all decrypted and compared against the plaintext-space result; `batch.zig` checks each slot against direct evaluation `m(ζ^e)`; an end-to-end multiply + relinearize + rotate at `params.secure(4096, 65537, .tc128)`; every `defaultPrimes` chain re-validated;
  - parameter and modulus refusals (`init` running `validate`, `Ntt.init` on a composite `q`, the `2^62` bounds, auxiliary primes equal to a main prime skipped).
- **Stack probe:** `src/stackprobe_test.zig` (`testkit.stackprobe`) checks that `keyGen`, `genRelinKey`, `genGaloisKey` (at `bfv_toy`), `decrypt` and `noiseBudget` leave no secret-key residue on the dead stack, at `bfv_toy` and at the security-grade set (ReleaseFast).
- **Fuzz:** `BFV_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]` (testkit driver, `src/fuzz_test.zig`, harness `bfv-codec`): damaged encodings of every codec kind and raw bytes; whatever decodes re-encodes to the same bytes; an in-suite reach test requires both outcomes.
- **ctgrind:** `src/ctgrind_harness.zig`, targets `keygen`, `encrypt`, `decrypt` (ReleaseFast; rows in `scripts/checks/ctgrind-expected.tsv`, run by `scripts/checks/ctgrind.sh`); the baseline-CPU variant is `CTGRIND_CPU=x86_64`. Source-level CT only, see *Threats / caveats*.
- **Mutation:** the whole-module run covers every non-test file (`modarith`, `ntt`, `rns`, `ring`, `encode`, `params`, `bfv`); comptime sizing, `gate.zig`, `bench.zig`, the ctgrind harness and the KAT data are not mutated. Three kinds of mutant: functional (one ReleaseSafe schemata build), burn-site (one `burn.run` per secret entry point, read by the stack probe, `DeadStackResidue`) and constant-time (judged by ctgrind only: `csub`'s and `subMod`'s `blackBox` removed, the `sampleTernary` trit select written as `if`/`else`; no functional test can see them).
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation run and the delta runs after it.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class B · oracle REDERIVED

- **Class B** — published cryptographic or algorithmic construction with published vectors.
- **Oracle REDERIVED** — an in-house oracle re-deriving the answer by a different route. Catches implementation typos; does NOT catch a shared misreading of the spec.

**What the tests actually contain.** NTT/RNS/BFV KAT vectors from independent Python re-derivation (SPEC.md)

## Backlog / deferred

Open items only. All are additive; none is a defect of what exists.

- **Fast RNS step for the multiply's input lift:** Halevi–Polyakov base conversion replacing `rns.Basis.convertExact` for the `[0,q)` CRT lift of the multiply's inputs. `mulBehz` itself needs no exact tensor and no big-integer division; that input lift is the only wide arithmetic left on the multiply path.
- **Rescale loop: restore vectorisation under the CT barrier (vector-select form):** since `csub`/`subMod` launder their mask, the `rescale/coeff` BEHZ-RNS micro-row of the opt-in bench reads 59.1 -> 131.9 ns at log2 q=36 and 1.25-1.33x slower at q=120..300 (`BFV_BENCH=1`, ReleaseFast, measured on a shared, noisy host; end-to-end HomMul not slower). Not done: one primitive, always constant-time; a vector-select form would let LLVM vectorise again without a branch. Re-measure on a quiet host first.

## Roadmap

- **Bootstrapping** (the depth-refresh step): the biggest deferred piece; the scheme is leveled, so the multiplicative depth is bounded by the parameter set's noise ledger. Project-size (weeks–months): needs digit extraction / homomorphic decryption circuits and a parameter regime large enough to run them.
- **BGV and CKKS** *(survey 2026-09-30)*: CKKS is what most SEAL/OpenFHE/Lattigo users actually run (real-number arithmetic, ML inference). Large (a month each: encoder, rescale, bootstrapping for CKKS); fits §2. Torn on whether this is "missing and it matters" for a BFV module — recorded here so the question is asked, not assumed. Project-size: a new scheme each, with its own encoder and noise model.
